messages:
Alyssa (Support): Hey team — Acme escalated: intermittent failures to payments.svc.acme.internal after a networking change last week; errors are TLS verify failures and occasional connection refused.
Ben (Acme): From our pod and laptop: `curl -v https://payments.svc.acme.internal/api/health` -> sometimes `curl: (7) Failed to connect`, sometimes `curl: (60) SSL: certificate problem: Invalid certificate chain`.
Mike (Infra): Do we have their VPC id and any recent Route53/resolver changes? Please paste dig + traceroute from inside the VPC (not a dev laptop).
Ben (Acme): Quick captures from two pods on different nodes below. They were taken within minutes of each other.
```
# pod on node-1
$ dig +short payments.svc.acme.internal @169.254.20.10
10.10.200.11
# pod on node-2
$ dig +short payments.svc.acme.internal @169.254.20.10
54.72.11.99
```
Jordan (SRE): That is the smoking gun — node-local resolver returning a private IP on one node and a public IP on another. Likely split-horizon (private hosted zone vs public record) or inconsistent resolver_rule forwarding (cross-account/TGW).
Alyssa (Support): Forcing curl to the public IP reproduces the public cert and a validity error:
```
$ curl -v --resolve payments.svc.acme.internal:443:54.72.11.99 https://payments.svc.acme.internal/
* Connected to payments.svc.acme.internal (54.72.11.99) port 443
* Server certificate: CN=payments.acme.com
* SSL certificate problem: certificate is not yet valid
```
Mike (Infra): Two likely failure vectors: (1) some queries resolve to the public IP, so clients hit the internet-facing endpoint which presents a different cert (CN mismatch / not-yet-valid), and egress/firewall differences can cause ECONNREFUSED; (2) node-local DNS (169.254.20.10) forwards conditionally to different upstreams (shared forwarders, TGW, or on-prem) leading to nondeterministic answers.
Jordan (SRE): Also check for stale delegations or resolver rules left after the Route53 rollback. Rollbacks can leave resolver_rule associations or TGW DNS settings in a weird state; caches can persist for hours.
Alyssa (Support): Proposed customer actions (RBAC-safe): run from pods on at least two different nodes: `dig @169.254.20.10 +trace payments.svc.acme.internal`, capture `nslookup payments.svc.acme.internal 169.254.20.10`, and run `tcpdump -n -s0 -vvv udp port 53 -c 200` on the node (we will provide an example DaemonSet wrapper if they cannot run tcpdump). Also share the hosted zone ID and any recent resolver_rule changes.
Ben (Acme): Will run those and paste results. FYI we rolled back a Route53 change last night — things looked stable for ~12h then started flipping back.
Mike (Infra): On our side: we'll enumerate associations for `svc.acme.internal`, check resolver_rule priorities and any TGW/VPC peering DNS forwarding. If traces show queries leaving 169.254.20.10 to a shared-account forwarder or TGW, that's the cause.
Jordan (SRE): Short-term mitigations: hostOverride in mesh or /etc/hosts in pods to pin the private IP, or temporarily allow egress to the public IP range to avoid ECONNREFUSED (not ideal). Long-term: ensure the private hosted zone is exclusively associated to the tenant VPC or remove conflicting resolver rules; issue internal certs with internal SANs (`payments.svc.acme.internal`) so cert checks fail more clearly when resolution leaks.
Alyssa (Support): Assigning actions: Mike (verify associations + infra checks), Jordan (diagnostic commands & RBAC-safe wrapper), Ben (run traces/tcpdump across nodes), Alyssa (customer comms and timeline). support-bot: ticket INC-2026-452 created and assigned.
Ben (Acme): Thanks — will post output in ~30m.
Jordan (SRE): When you post tcpdump, look for DNS queries forwarded from 169.254.20.10 to any IPs in the shared-services account, to on-prem forwarders, or to TGW addresses. That will explain node-specific hits to public vs private records.
Alyssa (Support): Great. I'll update the incident with next steps and close the loop once traces are in. :thumbsup:
